children.text: uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau /
children.translated_text: <s>Uśan</s> (desiring merit), <s>Vājaśravasa</s> indeed gave away all his possessions,

children.text: tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa // KaU_1.1 //
children.translated_text: He had a son named <s>Naciketā</s>. // KaU 1.1 //

children.text: taṃ ha kumāraṃ santaṃ dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhāviveśa /
children.translated_text: As the gifts were being led away, faith entered into him, though he was still a boy.

children.text: so 'manyata // KaU_1.2 //
children.translated_text: He reflected: // KaU 1.2 //

children.text: pītodakā jagdhatṛṇā dugdhadohā nirindriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: They have drunk their last water, eaten their last grass, given their last milk, and are devoid of vitality —

children.text: anandā nāma te lokās tān sa gacchati tā dadat // KaU_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Joyless indeed are those worlds; to them he goes who gives such (cows). // KaU 1.3 //

children.text: sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti /
children.translated_text: He said to his father: 'Father, to whom will you give me?'

children.text: dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyam /
children.translated_text: A second time, a third time (he asked).

children.text: taṃ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti // KaU_1.4 //
children.translated_text: He (the father) said to him: 'I give you to <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death).' // KaU 1.4 //

children.text: bahūnām emi prathamo bahūnām emi madhyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among many I go as the first, among many I go as the middling;

children.text: kiṃ svid yamasya kartavyaṃ yan mayādya kariṣyati // KaU_1.5 //
children.translated_text: What purpose of <s>Yama</s> could there be that he will accomplish through me today? // KaU 1.5 //

children.text: anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathāpare /
children.translated_text: Consider how it was with those who came before; look at how it is with those who came after —

children.text: sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam ivājāyate punaḥ // KaU_1.6 //
children.translated_text: A mortal ripens like grain and like grain is born again. // KaU 1.6 //

children.text: vaiśvānaraḥ praviśati atithir brāhmaṇo gṛhān /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (fire), a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> guest enters a house;

children.text: tasyaitāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam // KaU_1.7 //
children.translated_text: They offer him this pacification: 'Bring water, O son of <s>Vivasvat</s>!' // KaU 1.7 //

children.text: āśāpratīkṣe saṃgataṃ sūnṛtāṃ ca iṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūṃś ca sarvān /
children.translated_text: Hopes and expectations, the fruit of holy company and gracious speech, the merit of sacrifice and pious works, sons and cattle — all these

children.text: etad vṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso yasyānaśnan vasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe // KaU_1.8 //
children.translated_text: are destroyed for a man of little wisdom in whose house a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> dwells without eating. // KaU 1.8 //

children.text: tisro rātrīr yad avatsīr gṛhe me anaśnan brahmann atithir namasyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since you, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> guest worthy of reverence, have dwelt three nights in my house without eating,

children.text: namas te 'stu brahman svasti me 'stu tasmāt prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva // KaU_1.9 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to you, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>! May it be well with me! Therefore, choose three boons. // KaU 1.9 //

children.text: śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syād vītamanyur gautamo mābhi mṛtyo /
children.translated_text: May <s>Gautama</s> (my father) be of calmed resolve, of good mind, and free from anger toward me, O <s>Mṛtyu</s>;

children.text: tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ mābhivadet pratīta etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe // KaU_1.10 //
children.translated_text: may he greet me favorably when released by you — this I choose as the first of the three boons. // KaU 1.10 //

children.text: yathā purastād bhavitā pratīta auddālakir āruṇir matprasṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Auddālaki Āruṇi</s> (your father) will be as before, well-disposed, released by me;

children.text: sukhaṃ rātrīḥ śayitā vītamanyus tvāṃ dadṛśivān mṛtyumukhāt pramuktam // KaU_1.11 //
children.translated_text: he will sleep peacefully through the nights, free from anger, having seen you freed from the jaws of Death. // KaU 1.11 //

children.text: svarge loke na bhayaṃ kiṃcanāsti na tatra tvaṃ na jarayā bibheti /
children.translated_text: In the heavenly world there is no fear whatsoever; you (<s>Mṛtyu</s>) are not there, nor does one fear old age;

children.text: ubhe tīrtvā aśanāyāpipāse śokātigo modate svargaloke // KaU_1.12 //
children.translated_text: having crossed beyond both hunger and thirst, beyond sorrow, one rejoices in the heavenly world. // KaU 1.12 //

children.text: sa tvam agniṃ svargyam adhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi taṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam /
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Mṛtyu</s>, know the fire that leads to heaven; teach it to me who am full of faith.

children.text: svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajanta etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa // KaU_1.13 //
children.translated_text: The inhabitants of the heavenly world partake of immortality — this I choose as the second boon. // KaU 1.13 //

children.text: pra te bravīmi tad u me nibodha svargyam agniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan /
children.translated_text: I shall declare it to you — learn it from me, O <s>Naciketā</s>, understanding the heavenly fire;

children.text: anantalokāptim atho pratiṣṭhāṃ viddhi tvam etaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām // KaU_1.14 //
children.translated_text: know it as the attainment of the infinite world and as the foundation, hidden in the secret cave. // KaU 1.14 //

children.text: lokādim agniṃ tam uvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakā yāvatīr vā yathā vā /
children.translated_text: He told him of that fire, the beginning of the worlds — what the bricks are, how many, and in what manner;

children.text: sa cāpi tat pratyavadad yathoktam athāsya mṛtyuḥ punar āha tuṣṭaḥ // KaU_1.15 //
children.translated_text: and he (<s>Naciketā</s>) repeated it back as it was told. Then <s>Mṛtyu</s>, pleased, spoke again: // KaU 1.15 //

children.text: tam abravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The great soul (<s>Yama</s>), delighted, said to him: 'I give you yet another boon today.

children.text: tavaiva nāmnā bhavitāyam agniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemām anekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa // KaU_1.16 //
children.translated_text: This fire shall henceforth bear your name; and accept this manifold garland.' // KaU 1.16 //

children.text: triṇāciketas tribhir etya sandhiṃ trikarmakṛt tarati janmamṛtyū /
children.translated_text: He who has kindled the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire three times, having united with the three, performing the three-fold duty, crosses beyond birth and death;

children.text: brahmajajñaṃ devam īḍyaṃ viditvā nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti // KaU_1.17 //
children.translated_text: knowing the adorable god born of <s>Brahman</s> and realizing him, he attains this everlasting peace. // KaU 1.17 //

children.text: triṇāciketas trayam etad viditvā ya evaṃ vidvāṃś cinute nāciketam /
children.translated_text: He who, having kindled the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire three times and knowing these three, builds the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire altar thus —

children.text: sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya śokātigo modate svargaloke // KaU_1.18 //
children.translated_text: he, having cast off the bonds of death beforehand, passes beyond sorrow and rejoices in the heavenly world. // KaU 1.18 //

children.text: eṣa te 'gnir naciketaḥ svargyo yam avṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa /
children.translated_text: This, O <s>Naciketā</s>, is your heavenly fire which you chose as the second boon;

children.text: etam agniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsas tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva // KaU_1.19 //
children.translated_text: people will proclaim this fire as yours indeed. Choose the third boon, O <s>Naciketā</s>. // KaU 1.19 //

children.text: yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye astīty eke nāyam astīti caike /
children.translated_text: There is this doubt regarding a person who has died — some say he exists, others say he does not.

children.text: etad vidyām anuśiṣṭas tvayāhaṃ varāṇām eṣa varas tṛtīyaḥ // KaU_1.20 //
children.translated_text: I would know this, instructed by you — this is the third of my boons. // KaU 1.20 //

children.text: devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ purā na hi sujñeyam aṇur eṣa dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the gods had doubt about this in ancient times, for this <s>dharma</s> is not easily known — it is subtle.

children.text: anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva mā moparotsīr ati mā sṛjainam // KaU_1.21 //
children.translated_text: Choose another boon, O <s>Naciketā</s>; do not press me — release me from this. // KaU 1.21 //

children.text: devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ kila tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yan na sujñeyam āttha /
children.translated_text: Even the gods, you say, had doubt about this, and you yourself, O <s>Mṛtyu</s>, say it is not easily known.

children.text: vaktā cāsya tvādṛg anyo na labhyo nānyo varas tulya etasya kaścit // KaU_1.22 //
children.translated_text: No other teacher like you can be found for this — no other boon is equal to this one. // KaU 1.22 //

children.text: śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hastihiraṇyam aśvān /
children.translated_text: Choose sons and grandsons who shall live a hundred years, many cattle, elephants, gold, and horses;

children.text: bhūmer mahad āyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvad icchasi // KaU_1.23 //
children.translated_text: choose a vast domain on earth, and live yourself as many autumns as you wish. // KaU 1.23 //

children.text: etat tulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: If you think this an equal boon, choose wealth and long life;

children.text: mahābhūmau naciketas tvam edhi kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi // KaU_1.24 //
children.translated_text: be a ruler on the great earth, O <s>Naciketā</s> — I shall make you the enjoyer of all desires. // KaU 1.24 //

children.text: ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke sarvān kāmāṃś chandataḥ prārthayasva /
children.translated_text: Whatever desires are hard to attain in the mortal world — ask freely for all those desires.

children.text: imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here are these fair maidens with their chariots and musical instruments — such as these are not to be won by men.

children.text: ābhir matprattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketo maraṇaṃ mānuprākṣīḥ // KaU_1.25 //
children.translated_text: Be served by these whom I bestow upon you — O <s>Naciketā</s>, do not ask about death! // KaU 1.25 //

children.text: śvobhāvā martyasya yad antakaitat sarvendriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ /
children.translated_text: Ephemeral are these, O Death, and they wear out the vigor of all the senses of a mortal;

children.text: api sarvaṃ jīvitam alpam eva tavaiva vāhās tava nṛtyagīte // KaU_1.26 //
children.translated_text: even a full life is but short. Yours alone be the chariots, yours the dance and song! // KaU 1.26 //

children.text: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma cet tvā /
children.translated_text: A person cannot be satisfied by wealth. Shall we possess wealth when we have seen you?

children.text: jīviṣyāmo yāvad īśiṣyasi tvaṃ varas tu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva // KaU_1.27 //
children.translated_text: We shall live only as long as you shall rule. That boon alone is to be chosen by me. // KaU 1.27 //

children.text: ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan /
children.translated_text: Having come near to the undecaying immortals, what decaying mortal on this earth below, who understands,

children.text: abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodān atidīrghe jīvite ko rameta // KaU_1.28 //
children.translated_text: who reflects upon the pleasures of beauty and enjoyment, would delight in an exceedingly long life? // KaU 1.28 //

children.text: yasminn idaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo yat sāmparāye mahati brūhi nas tat /
children.translated_text: That about which they doubt, O <s>Mṛtyu</s> — what happens in the great passing beyond — tell us that.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ varo gūḍham anupraviṣṭo nānyaṃ tasmān naciketā vṛṇīte // KaU_1.29 //
children.translated_text: This boon that has entered deep into the mystery — no other than this does <s>Naciketā</s> choose. // KaU 1.29 //

children.text: anyac chreyo 'nyad utaiva preyas te ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṃ sinītaḥ /
children.translated_text: The good (<s>śreyas</s>) is one thing, and the pleasant (<s>preyas</s>) another; these two, having different ends, bind a person.

children.text: tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate 'rthād ya u preyo vṛṇīte // KaU_2.1 //
children.translated_text: It is well for him who chooses the good; he who chooses the pleasant falls short of the true goal. // KaU 2.1 //

children.text: śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau saṃparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ /
children.translated_text: Both the good and the pleasant approach a person; the wise one, examining them, distinguishes between them.

children.text: śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemād vṛṇīte // KaU_2.2 //
children.translated_text: The wise one chooses the good over the pleasant; the fool, out of greed and attachment, chooses the pleasant. // KaU 2.2 //

children.text: sa tvaṃ priyān priyarūpāṃś ca kāmān abhidhyāyan naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ /
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Naciketā</s>, having pondered the desires that are dear and appear delightful, have rejected them;

children.text: naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīm avāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ // KaU_2.3 //
children.translated_text: you have not taken this chain of wealth in which many mortals sink. // KaU 2.3 //

children.text: dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā /
children.translated_text: Far apart and leading in opposite directions are these two: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and what is known as <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).

children.text: vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo 'lolupanta // KaU_2.4 //
children.translated_text: I consider <s>Naciketā</s> as one who desires knowledge, for the many desires did not tempt you. // KaU 2.4 //

children.text: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Dwelling in the midst of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), yet thinking themselves wise and learned,

children.text: dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ // KaU_2.5 //
children.translated_text: the deluded wander about, going round and round, like the blind led by the blind. // KaU 2.5 //

children.text: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham /
children.translated_text: The hereafter never reveals itself to the careless one, deluded by the glamour of wealth.

children.text: ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punar vaśam āpadyate me // KaU_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Thinking 'this world alone exists, there is no other' — such a one falls again and again under my power. // KaU 2.6 //

children.text: śravaṇāyāpi bahubhir yo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ /
children.translated_text: That (<s>Ātman</s>) which many cannot even hear of, which many, even hearing, do not know —

children.text: āścaryo vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhā āścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ // KaU_2.7 //
children.translated_text: wonderful is the teacher, skillful is the one who obtains it; wonderful is the knower, instructed by the skillful. // KaU 2.7 //

children.text: na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: This (<s>Ātman</s>), when taught by an inferior person, is not easily understood, for it is thought of in many ways;

children.text: ananyaprokte gatir atra nāsty aṇīyān hy atarkyam aṇupramāṇāt // KaU_2.8 //
children.translated_text: unless taught by one who knows it as non-different (from oneself), there is no way to it, for it is subtler than the subtle, beyond reasoning. // KaU 2.8 //

children.text: naiṣā tarkeṇa matir āpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha /
children.translated_text: This understanding is not to be attained by reasoning; it is best understood, dear one, when taught by another (a true teacher).

children.text: yāṃ tvam āpaḥ satyadhṛtir batāsi tvādṛṅ no bhūyān naciketaḥ preṣṭā // KaU_2.9 //
children.translated_text: You have attained it, being firmly devoted to truth. May there be more questioners like you, O <s>Naciketā</s>, dear one! // KaU 2.9 //

children.text: jānāmy ahaṃ śevadhir ity anityaṃ na hy adhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: I know that what is called treasure is transient, for the eternal is not attained by things which are not eternal.

children.text: tato mayā nāciketaś cito 'gnir anityair dravyaiḥ prāptavān asmi nityam // KaU_2.10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire has been built by me with impermanent things, and I have attained the eternal. // KaU 2.10 //

children.text: kāmasya āptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ krator anantyam abhayasya pāram /
children.translated_text: The fulfillment of desire, the foundation of the world, the endlessness of ritual, the farther shore of fearlessness,

children.text: stomamahad urugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ // KaU_2.11 //
children.translated_text: the greatness of widespread praise, the vast foundation — having seen all this, O wise <s>Naciketā</s>, you have firmly rejected them. // KaU 2.11 //

children.text: taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍham anupraviṣṭaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam /
children.translated_text: That (<s>Ātman</s>), difficult to see, deeply hidden, set in the cave (of the heart), dwelling in the depth, primordial —

children.text: adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti // KaU_2.12 //
children.translated_text: knowing that god through the discipline of self-knowledge (<s>adhyātma-yoga</s>), the wise one leaves behind both joy and sorrow. // KaU 2.12 //

children.text: etac chrutvā saṃparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyam aṇum etam āpya /
children.translated_text: A mortal who has heard this and fully grasped it, who has drawn forth this subtle essence of <s>dharma</s> and attained it —

children.text: sa modate modanīyaṃ hi labdhvā vivṛtaṃ sadma naciketasaṃ manye // KaU_2.13 //
children.translated_text: he indeed rejoices, for he has obtained that which is worthy of rejoicing. I consider the abode to be wide open for <s>Naciketā</s>. // KaU 2.13 //

children.text: anyatra dharmād anyatrādharmād anyatrāsmāt kṛtākṛtāt /
children.translated_text: Other than <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), other than <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), other than what is done and not done here,

children.text: anyatra bhūtāc ca bhavyāc ca yat tat paśyasi tad vada // KaU_2.14 //
children.translated_text: other than what has been and what is yet to be — that which you see, tell me that. // KaU 2.14 //

children.text: sarve vedā yat padam āmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti /
children.translated_text: That goal which all the <s>Vedas</s> declare, which all austerities proclaim,

children.text: yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmi //
children.translated_text: desiring which, they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) — that state I shall declare to you in brief:

children.text: etad dhy evākṣaraṃ brahma etad dhy evākṣaraṃ param /
children.translated_text: This syllable is indeed <s>Brahman</s>; this syllable is indeed the Supreme;

children.text: etad dhy evākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yad icchati tasya tat // KaU_2.16 //
children.translated_text: having known this syllable, whatever one desires, that is his. // KaU_2.16 //

children.text: etad ālambanaṃ śreṣṭham etad ālambanaṃ param /
children.translated_text: This is the best support; this is the supreme support;

children.text: etad ālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate // KaU_2.17 //
children.translated_text: having known this support, one is magnified in the world of <s>Brahman</s>. // KaU_2.17 //

children.text: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin nāyaṃ kutaścin na babhūva kaścit /
children.translated_text: The wise one is not born, nor does he die; he did not come from anywhere, nor did he become anyone;

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre // KaU_2.18 //
children.translated_text: unborn, eternal, everlasting, primeval — he is not slain when the body is slain. // KaU_2.18 //

children.text: hantā cen manyate hantuṃ hataś cen manyate hatam /
children.translated_text: If the slayer thinks he slays, and if the slain thinks he is slain,

children.text: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate // KaU_2.19 //
children.translated_text: both of them do not understand — this one neither slays nor is slain. // KaU_2.19 //

children.text: aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmāsya jantor nihito guhāyām /
children.translated_text: Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great, the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is hidden in the cave of this living being;

children.text: tam akratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādān mahimānam ātmanaḥ // KaU_2.20 //
children.translated_text: one who is free from desire beholds the majesty of the <s>Ātman</s>, freed from sorrow, through the grace of the Creator. // KaU_2.20 //

children.text: āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Sitting, he travels far; lying down, he goes everywhere;

children.text: kas taṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ mad anyo jñātum arhati // KaU_2.21 //
children.translated_text: who other than I is worthy to know that God who rejoices and rejoices not? // KaU_2.21 //

children.text: aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu anavastheṣv avasthitam /
children.translated_text: Bodiless within bodies, stable among the unstable,

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // KaU_2.22 //
children.translated_text: the wise one, having known the great, all-pervading <s>Ātman</s>, does not grieve. // KaU_2.22 //

children.text: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena /
children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s> is not attained by discourse, nor by intellect, nor by much learning;

children.text: yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām // KaU_2.23 //
children.translated_text: he whom this [<s>Ātman</s>] chooses, by him alone is it attained — to him this <s>Ātman</s> reveals its own form. // KaU_2.23 //

children.text: nāvirato duścaritān nāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not one who has not ceased from evil conduct, nor one who is not tranquil, nor one who is not concentrated,

children.text: nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainam āpnuyāt // KaU_2.24 //
children.translated_text: nor one whose mind is not at peace — could attain this through knowledge alone. // KaU_2.24 //

children.text: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ /
children.translated_text: For whom both the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the <s>kṣatriya</s> are as food,

children.text: mṛtyur yasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ // KaU_2.25 //
children.translated_text: and death is the condiment — who truly knows where he is? // KaU_2.25 //

children.text: ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe /
children.translated_text: The two who drink <s>Ṛta</s> (truth), having entered the cave in the highest space, in the world of good deeds —

children.text: chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ // KaU_3.1 //
children.translated_text: the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> call them shadow and light, as do the householders who maintain the five fires and the three <s>Nāciketa</s> fires. // KaU_3.1 //

children.text: yaḥ setur ījānānām akṣaraṃ brahma yat param /
children.translated_text: May we be able to master the <s>Nāciketa</s> [fire], which is the bridge for those who sacrifice, which is the imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme,

children.text: abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketaṃ śakemahi // KaU_3.2 //
children.translated_text: the fearless, the far shore for those who wish to cross over. // KaU_3.2 //

children.text: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu /
children.translated_text: Know the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as the lord of the chariot, and the body as the chariot itself;

children.text: buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca // KaU_3.3 //
children.translated_text: know the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) as the charioteer, and the mind (<s>manas</s>) as the reins. // KaU_3.3 //

children.text: indriyāṇi hayān āhur viṣayāṃs teṣu gocarān /
children.translated_text: The senses, they say, are the horses; the sense-objects are the roads;

children.text: ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktety āhur manīṣiṇaḥ // KaU_3.4 //
children.translated_text: the wise call the <s>Ātman</s> united with the senses and the mind the enjoyer. // KaU_3.4 //

children.text: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty ayuktena manasā sadā /
children.translated_text: But one who is devoid of understanding, whose mind is always uncontrolled —

children.text: tasyendriyāṇy avaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ // KaU_3.5 //
children.translated_text: his senses are unmanageable, like the wild horses of a charioteer. // KaU_3.5 //

children.text: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā /
children.translated_text: But one who possesses understanding, whose mind is always controlled —

children.text: tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ // KaU_3.6 //
children.translated_text: his senses are manageable, like the good horses of a charioteer. // KaU_3.6 //

children.text: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty amanaskaḥ sadāśuciḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who is devoid of understanding, who is mindless and always impure —

children.text: na sa tat padam āpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati // KaU_3.7 //
children.translated_text: he does not reach that state, and falls into the cycle of rebirth (<s>saṃsāra</s>). // KaU_3.7 //

children.text: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who possesses understanding, who is mindful and always pure —

children.text: sa tu tat padam āpnoti yasmād bhūyo na jāyate // KaU_3.8 //
children.translated_text: he indeed reaches that state from which he is not born again. // KaU_3.8 //

children.text: vijñānasārathir yas tu manaḥ pragrahavān naraḥ /
children.translated_text: The man who has understanding as his charioteer and holds the reins of the mind firmly —

children.text: so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // KaU_3.9 //
children.translated_text: he reaches the end of the journey, that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // KaU_3.9 //

children.text: indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond the senses are the objects; beyond the objects is the mind;

children.text: manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ // KaU_3.10 //
children.translated_text: beyond the mind is the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>); beyond the intellect is the great <s>Ātman</s>. // KaU_3.10 //

children.text: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond the great is the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>); beyond the unmanifest is the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person);

children.text: puruśān na paraṃ kiṃcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ // KaU_3.11 //
children.translated_text: beyond the <s>Puruṣa</s> there is nothing — that is the culmination, that is the highest goal. // KaU_3.11 //

children.text: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s>, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth;

children.text: dṛṣyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ // KaU_3.12 //
children.translated_text: but it is seen by the subtle seers through the sharp, refined intellect. // KaU_3.12 //

children.text: yacched vāṅmanasī prājñas tad yacchej jñāna ātmani /
children.translated_text: The wise one should merge speech into the mind, and that [mind] he should merge into the knowing self;

children.text: jñānam ātmani mahati niyacchet tad yacchec chānta ātmani // KaU_3.13 //
children.translated_text: knowledge he should merge into the great <s>Ātman</s>, and that he should merge into the peaceful Self. // KaU_3.13 //

children.text: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata /
children.translated_text: Arise! Awake! Having attained the excellent [teachers], understand!

children.text: kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathas tat kavayo vadanti // KaU_3.14 //
children.translated_text: The edge of a razor is sharp and difficult to cross — the poets say that path is hard to traverse. // KaU_3.14 //

children.text: aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavac ca yat /
children.translated_text: That which is without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable, and likewise without taste, eternal, without scent,

children.text: anādy anantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tan mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate // KaU_3.15 //
children.translated_text: without beginning, without end, beyond the great, unchanging — having discerned that, one is freed from the jaws of death. // KaU_3.15 //

children.text: nāciketam upākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktaṃ sanātanam /
children.translated_text: The ancient story of <s>Naciketas</s>, told by <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) —

children.text: uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate // KaU_3.16 //
children.translated_text: having told and heard it, the wise one is magnified in the world of <s>Brahman</s>. // KaU_3.16 //

children.text: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi /
children.translated_text: Whoever recites this supreme secret in an assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tad ānantyāya kalpate /
children.translated_text: or devoutly at the time of the <s>śrāddha</s> (funeral rites) — that leads to infinity,

children.text: tad ānantyāya kalpata iti // KaU_3.17 //
children.translated_text: that leads to infinity. // KaU_3.17 //

children.text: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūs tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman /
children.translated_text: The self-existent one (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>) pierced the openings [of the senses] outward; therefore one sees outward, not the inner <s>Ātman</s>;

children.text: kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag ātmānam aikṣad āvṛttacakṣur amṛtatvam icchan // KaU_4.1 //
children.translated_text: some wise one, desiring immortality, turned his gaze inward and saw the inner <s>Ātman</s>. // KaU_4.1 //

children.text: parācaḥ kāmān anuyanti bālās te mṛtyor yanti vitatasya pāśam /
children.translated_text: The childish pursue outward desires and walk into the snare of death spread wide;

children.text: atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvam adhruveṣv iha na prārthayante // KaU_4.2 //
children.translated_text: but the wise, having known that the eternal is not [found] among the impermanent things here, do not pray for anything. // KaU_4.2 //

children.text: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśīṃś ca maithunān /
children.translated_text: That by which one perceives form, taste, smell, sounds, and touches of union —

children.text: etenaiva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate //
children.translated_text: by this very [<s>Ātman</s>] indeed one knows — what remains here [that is not known]?

children.text: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati /
children.translated_text: That by which one perceives both the dream state and the waking state —

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // KaU_4.4 //
children.translated_text: having known that great, all-pervading <s>Ātman</s>, the wise one does not grieve. // KaU_4.4 //

children.text: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvam antikāt /
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Ātman</s>, the honey-eater, the living self, close at hand,

children.text: īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate //
children.translated_text: the lord of past and future — from that he does not shrink away.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātam adbhyaḥ pūrvam ajāyata /
children.translated_text: He who was born before, born from <s>tapas</s> (austerity), born before the waters,

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhir vyapaśyata //
children.translated_text: who, having entered the cave, stands there, who is seen through beings —

children.text: yā prāṇena saṃbhavati aditir devatāmayī /
children.translated_text: She who comes into being with <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), <s>Aditi</s>, full of the gods,

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhir vyajāyata //
children.translated_text: who, having entered the cave, stands there, who was born through beings —

children.text: araṇyor nihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Jātavedas</s> (the fire of knowledge), placed in the two fire-sticks, well-guarded like a fetus by pregnant women —

children.text: divediva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhir haviṣmadbhir manuṣyebhir agniḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Agni</s> (fire) is to be worshipped day after day by waking men who bear oblations.

children.text: yataś codeti sūryo astaṃ yatra ca gacchati /
children.translated_text: That from which the sun rises and into which it sets —

children.text: taṃ devāḥ sarve arpitās tad u nātyeti kaścana //
children.translated_text: in that are all the gods established; no one goes beyond that.

children.text: yad eveha tad amutra yad amutra tad anv iha /
children.translated_text: What is here, that is there; what is there, that is also here;

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati // KaU_4.10 //
children.translated_text: he who sees any difference here goes from death to death. // KaU_4.10 //

children.text: manasaivedam āptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: By the mind alone is this to be realized — there is no diversity here whatsoever;

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati // KaU_4.11 //
children.translated_text: he who sees any difference here goes from death to death. // KaU_4.11 //

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), of the size of a thumb, dwells in the middle of the self,

children.text: īśāno bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate //
children.translated_text: lord of past and future — from that one does not shrink away.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotir iva adhūmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the size of a thumb, like a flame without smoke,

children.text: īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ //
children.translated_text: lord of past and future — he is the same today and he shall be the same tomorrow.

children.text: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati /
children.translated_text: As rainwater fallen on a rugged height runs down among the mountains,

children.text: evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃs tān evānu vidhāvati // KaU_4.14 //
children.translated_text: so one who sees <s>dharmas</s> (principles) as separate runs after them in the same way. // KaU_4.14 //

children.text: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddham āsiktaṃ tādṛg eva bhavati /
children.translated_text: As pure water poured into pure water becomes just the same,

children.text: evaṃ muner vijānata ātmā bhavati gautama // KaU_4.15 //
children.translated_text: so becomes the self of the sage who knows, O <s>Gautama</s>. // KaU_4.15 //

children.text: puram ekādaśadvāram ajasyāvakracetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The city of eleven gates belonging to the unborn one, whose thought is not crooked —

children.text: anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaś ca vimucyate //
children.translated_text: having governed [it], one does not grieve; and being liberated, one is indeed freed.

children.text: haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasad dhotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat /
children.translated_text: As the swan (<s>haṃsa</s>) dwelling in the pure [sky], as <s>Vasu</s> dwelling in the atmosphere, as the priest (<s>hotā</s>) dwelling at the altar, as the guest dwelling in the house,

children.text: nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat // KaU_5.2 //
children.translated_text: dwelling among men, dwelling in the noble, dwelling in truth, dwelling in the sky — born of water, born of cattle, born of truth, born of the mountain — that great Truth. // KaU_5.2 //

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam unnayati apānaṃ pratyag asyati /
children.translated_text: He leads the <s>prāṇa</s> (out-breath) upward and casts the <s>apāna</s> (in-breath) downward;

children.text: madhye vāmanam āsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate // KaU_5.3 //
children.translated_text: the adorable one seated in the middle — all the gods worship him. // KaU_5.3 //

children.text: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: When this embodied one who dwells in the body

children.text: dehād vimucyamānasya kim atra pariśiṣyate //
children.translated_text: is released, when he is freed from the body — what remains here?

children.text: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana /
children.translated_text: No mortal lives by <s>prāṇa</s> (out-breath) or by <s>apāna</s> (in-breath);

children.text: itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminn etāv upāśritau // KaU_5.5 //
children.translated_text: they live by something else, on which these two depend. // KaU_5.5 //

children.text: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam /
children.translated_text: Come, I shall declare to you this secret, the eternal <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama // KaU_5.6 //
children.translated_text: and what becomes of the <s>Ātman</s> after reaching death, O <s>Gautama</s>. // KaU_5.6 //

children.text: yonim anye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some embodied souls enter a womb for embodiment;

children.text: sthāṇum anye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam // KaU_5.7 //
children.translated_text: others enter stationary [forms] — according to their <s>karma</s> (deeds) and according to their knowledge. // KaU_5.7 //

children.text: ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Puruṣa</s> who is awake among those who sleep, fashioning desire after desire —

children.text: tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate /
children.translated_text: that indeed is the Pure; that is <s>Brahman</s>; that indeed is called the Immortal;

children.text: tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana //
children.translated_text: in him all worlds are established — no one goes beyond him. //

children.text: agnir yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva /
children.translated_text: Just as fire, though one, having entered the world, assumes form after form corresponding to each form,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca // KaU_5.9 //
children.translated_text: so too the one inner <s>Ātman</s> (Self) of all beings assumes form after form corresponding to each, and yet is beyond [them]. [KaU 5.9]

children.text: vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva /
children.translated_text: Just as wind, though one, having entered the world, assumes form after form corresponding to each form,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca // KaU_5.10 //
children.translated_text: so too the one inner <s>Ātman</s> (Self) of all beings assumes form after form corresponding to each, and yet is beyond [them]. [KaU 5.10]

children.text: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣur na lipyate cākṣuṣair bāhyadoṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not tainted by the external defects [seen by] the eyes,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ // KaU_5.11 //
children.translated_text: so too the one inner <s>Ātman</s> (Self) of all beings is not tainted by the suffering of the world, being external [to it]. [KaU 5.11]

children.text: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti /
children.translated_text: The one controller, the inner <s>Ātman</s> (Self) of all beings, who makes the one form manifold—

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām // KaU_5.12 //
children.translated_text: the wise who perceive Him as abiding in the self, to them belongs eternal bliss, not to others. [KaU 5.12]

children.text: nityo 'nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān /
children.translated_text: The Eternal among the non-eternal, the Conscious among the conscious, the One among the many, who fulfills desires—

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣaṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām // KaU_5.13 //
children.translated_text: the wise who perceive Him as abiding in the self, to them belongs eternal peace, not to others. [KaU 5.13]

children.text: tad etad iti manyante 'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: 'This is That'—thus they regard the indescribable, supreme bliss.

children.text: kathaṃ nu tad vijānīyāṃ kim u bhāti vibhāti vā // KaU_5.14 //
children.translated_text: How then may I know That? Does it shine, or does it shine forth? [KaU 5.14]

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ /
children.translated_text: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine—how then this fire?

children.text: tam eva bhāntam anu bhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti // KaU_5.15 //
children.translated_text: Him alone shining, everything shines after; by His radiance all this is illumined. [KaU 5.15]

children.text: ūrdhvamūlo avākśākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ /
children.translated_text: With roots above and branches below, this is the eternal <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree).

children.text: tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate /
children.translated_text: That indeed is the Pure, that is <s>Brahman</s>, that alone is called the Immortal.

children.text: tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana //
children.translated_text: In That all worlds are established, and none goes beyond That.

children.text: yad idaṃ kiṃca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam /
children.translated_text: Whatever there is—this whole world—having issued forth from <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath), moves [within it].

children.text: mahad bhayaṃ vajram udyataṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti // KaU_6.2 //
children.translated_text: The great fear, like an upraised thunderbolt—those who know This become immortal. [KaU 6.2]

children.text: bhayād asyāgnis tapati bhayāt tapati sūryaḥ /
children.translated_text: From fear of Him, fire burns; from fear, the sun gives heat;

children.text: bhayād indraś ca vāyuś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ // KaU_6.3 //
children.translated_text: from fear, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, and Death, the fifth, run [to their appointed tasks]. [KaU 6.3]

children.text: iha ced aśakad boddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one is able to realize [<s>Brahman</s>] here, before the dissolution of the body,

children.text: tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate // KaU_6.4 //
children.translated_text: then one becomes fit for embodiment in the created worlds. [KaU 6.4]

children.text: yathādarśe tathātmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke /
children.translated_text: As in a mirror, so in one's own self; as in a dream, so in the world of the ancestors;

children.text: yathāpsu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayor iva brahmaloke // KaU_6.5 //
children.translated_text: as [seen reflected] in water, so in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>; as [the distinction between] shadow and light, so in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>. [KaU 6.5]

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvam udayāstamayau ca yat /
children.translated_text: The separate nature of the senses, and [the fact] that their arising and ceasing—

children.text: pṛthag utpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // KaU_6.6 //
children.translated_text: knowing that they arise separately, the wise one does not grieve. [KaU 6.6]

children.text: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Beyond the senses is the mind; beyond the mind is the <s>sattva</s> (intellect), the highest;

children.text: sattvād adhi mahānātmā mahato 'vyaktam uttamam // KaU_6.7 //
children.translated_text: beyond the <s>sattva</s> is the great <s>Ātman</s> (Self); beyond the great is the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest), the highest. [KaU 6.7]

children.text: avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako 'liṅga eva ca /
children.translated_text: Beyond the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest) is the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person), all-pervading and without any mark;

children.text: yaṃ jñātvā mucyate jantur amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati // KaU_6.8 //
children.translated_text: knowing whom, a being is liberated and attains immortality. [KaU 6.8]

children.text: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam /
children.translated_text: His form does not stand within the range of vision; no one sees Him with the eye.

children.text: hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti // KaU_6.9 //
children.translated_text: He is apprehended by the heart, by insight, by the mind—those who know This become immortal. [KaU 6.9]

children.text: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha /
children.translated_text: When the five [organs of] knowledge come to rest together with the mind,

children.text: buddhiś ca na viceṣṭati tām āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim // KaU_6.10 //
children.translated_text: and the intellect does not stir—that, they say, is the highest state. [KaU 6.10]

children.text: tāṃ yogam iti manyante sthirām indriyadhāraṇām /
children.translated_text: That firm holding of the senses they regard as <s>Yoga</s>;

children.text: apramattas tadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau // KaU_6.11 //
children.translated_text: one becomes vigilant at that time, for <s>Yoga</s> is both the origin and the dissolution. [KaU 6.11]

children.text: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā /
children.translated_text: He cannot be attained by speech, nor by the mind, nor by the eye.

children.text: astīti bruvato 'nyatra kathaṃ tad upalabhyate // KaU_6.12 //
children.translated_text: How can He be realized by anyone other than one who says 'He is'? [KaU 6.12]

children.text: astīty evopalabdhavyas tattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: He is to be realized as 'He is,' and also through the true nature of both [aspects];

children.text: astīty evopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati // KaU_6.13 //
children.translated_text: to one who has realized Him as 'He is,' His true nature becomes clear. [KaU 6.13]

children.text: yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ /
children.translated_text: When all the desires that dwell in the heart are released,

children.text: atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnute // KaU_6.14 //
children.translated_text: then the mortal becomes immortal—here one attains <s>Brahman</s>. [KaU 6.14]

children.text: yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When all the knots of the heart are severed here,

children.text: atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty etāvad dhy anuśāsanam // KaU_6.15 //
children.translated_text: then the mortal becomes immortal—this much is the teaching. [KaU 6.15]

children.text: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā /
children.translated_text: There are a hundred and one channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>) of the heart; of them, one passes out through the crown of the head.

children.text: tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavati // KaU_6.16 //
children.translated_text: Going upward through that, one attains immortality; the others, going in various directions, serve for departure [in other ways]. [KaU 6.16]

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) of the size of a thumb, the inner <s>Ātman</s> (Self), is always seated in the heart of beings.

children.text: taṃ svāc charīrāt pravṛhen muñjād iveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa /
children.translated_text: One should draw Him out from one's own body, as one draws the stalk from a <s>muñja</s> grass, with firmness.

children.text: taṃ vidyāc chukram amṛtaṃ taṃ vidyāc chukram amṛtam iti // KaU_6.17 //
children.translated_text: One should know Him as the Pure, the Immortal—one should know Him as the Pure, the Immortal. [KaU 6.17]

children.text: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo 'tha labdhvā vidyām etāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Naciketas</s>, having received this knowledge taught by <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), and the entire method of <s>Yoga</s>,

children.text: brahmaprāpto virajo 'bhūd vimṛtyur anyo 'py evaṃ yo vid adhyātmam eva // KaU_6.18 //
children.translated_text: attained <s>Brahman</s> and became free from passion and free from death—and so shall any other who thus knows the inner Self. [KaU 6.18]
